advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_argv` scan list or tuple argv passed to a git-named helper even when the list does not start with "git", and add a reporting case like `_git(["show", f"{rev}:{path}"], root)`.
evidence:
tests/unit/test_rev_path_read_guard.py (diff): `if call.args and isinstance(call.args[0], (ast.List, ast.Tuple)):
        tokens = list(call.args[0].elts)
        if not tokens or _literal(tokens[0]) != "git":
            return None`
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:59: def _git(args: list[str], repo_root: str) -> str | None:

Absence: nothing falls back to the function-name heuristic (`"git" in name.lower().split("_")`) when the list does not start with "git". That shape is skipped silently instead of being scanned from its first literal verb.
advisory.finding: The new rev:path guard misses list-argv git helpers. When a call's first argument is a list or tuple whose first element is not the literal "git", `_argv` returns None and the call is never checked. src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py already has a helper of this shape: `_git(args: list[str], repo_root)`, called as `_git(["show", ...], root)`. A future `_git(["show", f"{rev}:{path}"], root)` there would bring the Windows MAX_PATH bug back while the guard still passes.
scenarios: A developer adds `_git(["show", f"{ref}:{path}"], root)` in build_drift.py (or another list-argv helper). The guard reports no findings, and the read fails on Windows when cwd plus the argument passes MAX_PATH.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_argv`, when the first argument is a List or Tuple whose first element is not "git", check the callee name with the existing git-name heuristic. If it matches, use the list's elements as tokens instead of returning None. Add `'_git(["show", f"{rev}:{path}"], root)'` to `test_the_scan_reports_each_unsafe_shape` and `'_git(["show", "-s", "--format=%cs", sha], root)'` to the safe shapes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness check to `test_no_revision_read_passes_a_rev_path_without_double_dash`: each `_SCANNED` directory exists and a non-zero number of .py files was scanned.
evidence: tests/unit/test_rev_path_read_guard.py:154-157: `for top in _SCANNED:` / `for path in sorted((root / top).rglob("*.py")):` / `findings += scan_source(...)`

No check anywhere that a scanned directory exists or that at least one file was parsed. `Path.rglob` on a missing directory yields nothing, so 'no unsafe reads' and 'scanned nothing' give the same pass.
advisory.finding: The real-tree guard test asserts that findings are absent and never checks that the scanner read anything. If `src/rebar` or `scripts` is moved or renamed, or `_ROOT` resolves to the wrong directory, `rglob` returns nothing and the test passes without scanning a single file.
scenarios: A refactor moves the package (e.g. src/rebar -> src/rebar_core) or the test file is relocated so `parents[2]` is no longer the repo root: the guard stays green and an unsafe `git show <rev>:<path>` reintroduced later goes undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have `scan_tree` also return or count the files it parsed, then in the test add `assert all((_ROOT / top).is_dir() for top in _SCANNED)` and `assert scanned > 0` before `assert not findings`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Optionally add a case that calls check_complexity_baseline's main-baseline read (with REPO_ROOT monkeypatched to a fixture repo) instead of re-running git in the test.
evidence: tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py:782-787: the test runs `["git", "show", f"{rev}:.github/complexity-baseline.json"]` itself rather than calling the lock-fetch function
tests/unit/test_rev_path_reads_long_cwd.py _CASES lists only product modules (_init_ensures, init, reclaim_publish, bridge_fsck, _opcert_gate_config, compat, project_ensures, engine_comparison)
advisory.finding: The long-cwd behavioural test drives only the 12 product reads. The 4 changed script reads have no runtime case past MAX_PATH; only the static guard covers them. One is the complexity-baseline lock read, which fails closed. The existing test of that path (test_complexity_baseline.py) builds its own `git show` call instead of running the production read.
scenarios: On Windows, check_complexity_baseline runs from a REPO_ROOT where len(REPO_ROOT)+1+len('<40-hex>:.github/complexity-baseline.json') >= 260, and a future edit brings back a `git show` read. Only the static AST guard would catch it, and only if the argv shape stays visible to it.
